samples: This program fetches the current weather for Berlin's fixed coordinates from the Open-Meteo service over HTTP, parses the JSON reply, and prints one line with the temperature (in °C) and wind speed (in km/h). If the request fails or the reply isn't in the expected shape, it stops with a labelled error (unreachable or bad response) instead of printing anything. It only reads from the network and writes to the console, but the city is hard-coded and `main` requests HTTP access to any host, even though the fetch helper itself is limited to the Open-Meteo host, so it works best as a small demo or starting point rather than a configurable tool.

This program makes one request to the Open-Meteo API for Berlin's fixed coordinates, parses the JSON reply, and prints the current temperature (in °C) and wind speed (in km/h) to the console. Network and failure behavior: the fetching function is limited to api.open-meteo.com, but `main` asks for unrestricted HTTP access, and any failure is reported as either "unreachable" or "bad response". It takes no input, so it is a handy small example or starting point rather than a general weather tool, although the fetch function itself works for any coordinates.

This program makes one request to the Open-Meteo weather service for Berlin's fixed coordinates, reads the current temperature and wind speed from the JSON reply, and prints them as a single line (temperature in °C, wind in km/h). If the network call fails or the reply isn't the expected shape, it stops with a clear "unreachable" or "bad response" error instead of printing anything. It is hardcoded to Berlin and takes no input, so you would need to change the coordinates to use it for another city, and it needs console and internet access to run.

This program asks the free Open-Meteo web service for Berlin's current weather and prints one line with the temperature in °C and the wind speed in km/h. The coordinates are fixed in the program, so using another city means editing it. It only reads from the network (the API host plus the console output) and writes nothing to disk, and if the request or the parsing of the reply fails, it stops and reports the problem as either "unreachable" or "bad response".

This program makes one request to the Open-Meteo API for Berlin's current conditions and prints a single line with the temperature in °C and the wind speed in km/h. If the request or the reading of the response fails, it stops with an error that says whether the service was unreachable or returned something unexpected. It is hardcoded to Berlin with no input, and it needs console and network access, with the network permission on its entry point left broader than the one API host it actually contacts.
